prs.title: Document side-bias experiments and curve/slope architecture options
prs.body:
Records reproducible longer-route and centered side-bias experiments, plots, the bounded architecture review, complete sprint journal, scope audit and handoff. Reconciles stale architecture/feature-plan status with implemented behavior and limitations.

No new slider behavior or slope algorithm ships here. The remaining UX decision is coupled strength/bias with original geometry at center versus separate strength and side-bias controls. Side orientation, junction-as-split semantics, and combined curve/slope constraints remain open.

Validation: combined stack code, scripts, tests and capture blobs match f3998ae exactly; only status documentation and the packaging note differ. Geometry suites passed on the split checkpoint and final stack, 31 Python tests passed, and bridge API verification passed. Native results are prior sprint captures, not new live tests. Two strict millimeter-drift failures and unavailable crossing coverage remain explicit.

Stacked on interior-junction smoothing; merge last.

Original incremental experiments (including unsuccessful approaches) remain intact in the [sprint history archive](https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/tree/dan/autonomous-regressions). Review branches organize final snapshots without rewriting that history.

prs.title: Preserve native connections through interior junction smoothing
prs.body:
Adds experimental Debug interior-junction smoothing with section fits around fixed junction attachments. Bounded common tangent rotation preserves the selected branches' relative angle while exact native directed connection sets gate Apply. Missing, stale or ambiguous preview mappings remain rejected. Endpoint rail validation now also rejects added connections instead of accepting a subset.

Includes failed fixed-handle and length-only experiments, composition-curvature analysis, prefab-limit evidence and successful common-rotation captures. Unselected incident curves are not edited; junction-as-split remains unsupported.

Validation: final geometry executable and all 31 targeted Python tests passed. Sprint native preview/Apply passed for an interior four-way road and a path through two highway merges. The rail merge preserves all four connections after +2/+3 degree rotations and matches preview on Apply, but its strict test still FAILS for 5.17 mm native node-center drift. This is not hidden by a relaxed tolerance.

**Debug-only:** Release retains interior rejection. Release/Burst execution, vehicle routing, non-merging crossings and broad visual quality remain unverified. Full Debug build/deployment passed during the sprint; packaging did not deploy.

prs.title: Add pinned split points with shared planar tangents
prs.body:
Smooth Curve now lets players pin eligible intermediate nodes from a UI list and smooth each section with a shared planar tangent at ordinary splits. Adds independently tested geometry and guarded NetworkTools automation for the bridge's nt_split command.

A split is a hard constraint: pin position and planar G1 continuity apply even at strength zero, so an existing kink can change at zero. No-split zero remains identity. Junction nodes cannot be selected as ordinary splits. Topology and node/control elevations are preserved by the transform.

Validation: the standalone split PR geometry executable passed during packaging. Sprint native preview and Apply checks passed for two rail splits at 0/0.5/1 and two road splits at 1, including 16 road movements. The one-split case preserves the join/connections but still FAILS the strict fixed-center test for approximately 3 mm native outer-junction drift; tolerance was not weakened. Human UI validation and Release/Burst remain pending.

Stacked on regression infrastructure; merge in order. Live automation requires the companion bridge PR.

prs.title: Add repeatable toy-save regressions and semantic lane checks
prs.body:
Adds a guarded regression runner that verifies known toy baselines, resolves fresh entities after reload, creates unique checkpoints, polls fresh previews and independently checks permanent Apply results. Lane checks compare directed semantic transitions and physical lane mappings, including direct joins and U-turns; connection counts alone do not pass.

Includes reload/checkpoint helpers, native slip-fixture construction, baseline fixtures, captured observations and failed construction evidence. Scripts require explicit mutation flags and reject uncertain state; they do not overwrite original saves or force-kill the game. Optional split/interior fixtures need the later feature PRs.

Validation: 31 targeted Python tests passed across the completed stack, including six runner, five lane-oracle and two reload tests. Sprint captures cover rail, road, highway on/off ramps and a limited two-edge slip bypass. This does not establish vehicle routing or visual quality. Non-merging rail crossings remain untested because the available rail prefabs were locked.

First NetworkTools PR in the stack; contains no runtime mod changes.

prs.title: Enable guarded autonomous Smooth Curve control and record live validation
prs.body:
## Behavior

Adds a Debug-only, versioned bridge adapter for activating Smooth Curve, selecting live endpoint nodes, adjusting strength, clearing selection, and requesting Apply through the existing tool paths. Session/revision checks reject stale commands; Apply additionally requires the current verified preview submission and unchanged original inputs. Apply acceptance is distinguished from completion.

Parent #5 has merged. This PR now targets main and contains only the subsequent automation milestone. Requires the matching bridge automation commands in the companion milestone PR.

## Validation

- Full Debug build, postprocessing, UI build and local deployment passed; geometry test executable passed.
- Live paused toy rail case: autonomous launch/load, tool activation, four-node selection, strength 0.5 then 0.8, and Apply completed.
- Stale revision and stale preview-submission requests were rejected.
- Independent captures: exactly three selected edges changed; all four directed rail connections preserved; incident permanent curve control points exactly matched preview. Maintainer visual inspection was positive.
- Reusable capture verifier and source evidence are committed under scripts/ and NetworkTools.docs/session-notes/.

## Limits

One live rail case, not broad junction coverage. Native rebuild readiness remains bounded experimental validation; interior-junction restrictions remain. Adapter is absent from Release. Clear, malformed inputs and disabled-control/STOP cases need wider live coverage. Activates an already loaded mod; it does not enable a playset entry. Existing unrelated UI package-lock change is excluded.

prs.title: Add junction diagnostics, captured rail evidence, and offline constraint prototypes
prs.body:
Smooth Curve junction failures need identifiable rejection reasons and native connection evidence before expanding supported selections. This adds rejection diagnostics and offline trace replay, captures working/broken rail merges, and prototypes constraints that distinguish preserving observed connections from explicitly repairing missing ones.

Includes reusable analysis/tests, actual-prefab-limit investigation, preview/rebuild timing findings, setup checks for our diagnostic bridge fork and coding-agent plugin, and session notes preserving unsuccessful experiments. Signed-length smoothing and split points remain exploratory; interior-junction rejection is retained.

Verification recorded during development: 16 Python tests plus geometry replay/build checks described in the session notes. In the latest supervised endpoint-junction test, all four directed rail connections survived Apply and all three incident curves matched preview controls exactly at captured precision; the user confirmed the visual result. This does not establish train traversal, general junction support, or native validation readiness. No fresh build/deployment was needed for this publication-only change.

The bridge is a development diagnostic dependency, not a runtime requirement for ordinary NetworkTools users. Its newest connected-preview resolver still needs deployment and live validation. Runtime junction smoothing remains deliberately limited pending that evidence.

prs.title: Enable experimental Smooth Curve with shared target geometry
prs.body:
## Behavior

Enable Smooth Curve using the existing node selection, preview, smoothing slider, and Apply workflow. Distorted interior endpoints previously kept their offsets even when handles were smoothed, leaving doglegs intact. The new experimental algorithm constructs one planar boundary cubic and moves interior nodes, segment endpoints, and handles together toward exact subcurves of that target.

Preserves topology, node/control-point elevations, outer endpoints, and selection boundary nodes. Handles reversed edge traversal and rejects unsuitable selections without publishing partial geometry. Adds job-lifetime synchronization and Debug-only JSON geometry traces.

## Scope and limitations

- Positive-strength selections with interior junctions or backward node chords are rejected. Junction support is follow-up work.
- A single cubic is an experimental target policy for simple paths, not general route preservation. No obstacle avoidance, movement cap, or complete intersection checks.
- Preserved Y coordinates do not guarantee unchanged grades or vertical tangent continuity.
- Includes the isolated upstream slope-preview elevation fix, cherry-picked with attribution from aa6e5428ad9be992d5a104b55b40445236eb0724.
- Preserves the incremental experiments, captured geometry fixture, plotting/replay tools, session notes, and AGENTS.md documentation workflow.

## Verification

- External geometry tests pass, including captured-path replay against production math, slider sweep, traversal reversal, boundary preservation, and rejected inputs/junctions.
- Full Debug and Release builds pass, including postprocessing, UI build, deployment, and Windows Burst compilation. Debug deployed last.
- Maintainer reports successful smoothing of heavily distorted endpoints and handles. Real-city elevated-rail screenshots show improved alignment and a final Apply view matching the preview.
- Train traversal, save/reload, and Release runtime execution remain unverified.

See NetworkTools.docs/session-notes/2026-09-26-1806.md for the experiment history and measured results.

prs.title: Add standalone curve geometry fitting and external checks
prs.body:
Adds a game-independent horizontal node-position fitter as the numerical foundation for Smooth Curve. It minimizes displacement plus weighted second differences on original chord-length stations, with fixed endpoints and optional interior pins, using an allocation-free banded Cholesky solver.

The source compiles into the mod but is not called by any tool. Smooth Curve remains disabled. This does not yet reconstruct Bezier handles, constrain endpoint tangents, prevent all self-intersections, or validate game integration.

Validation:
- Dependency-free .NET 8 executable checks passed in Release: analytic solution, uneven spacing, fixed points, zero strength, zigzag reduction, reversal/translation/rotation invariance, long-path objective stationarity, and invalid inputs.
- Full CS2 Debug build, postprocessing, UI build, and local deployment passed (37 warnings, zero errors).
- Burst execution and in-game geometry behavior remain unverified.

Run geometry checks with `dotnet run --project NetworkTools.Geometry.Tests/NetworkTools.Geometry.Tests.csproj --configuration Release`. The objective, unsafe buffer contract, and limitations are documented in NetworkTools.docs/curve-geometry.md.
